title: Fission & fusion
examples: What is the difference between fission and fusion?
How do stars create energy using these processes?
Can we use fusion power on Earth?

explain.say: Today we explore nuclear energy from fission and fusion. We will see how these processes work.
Fission is when a very large atom splits into smaller parts. This splitting releases a large amount of energy.
Fusion is the opposite process; it joins two small atomic nuclei together. This joining also releases massive amounts of energy.
A chain reaction happens when the energy released from one split causes more splits. This reaction can continue on its own.
Nuclear reactors use controlled fission chain reactions to generate electricity. They use special materials to manage the reaction.
Stars create energy through sustained fusion reactions. They are essentially giant, natural fusion reactors.

faq.q: What is the main difference between fission and fusion?
faq.a: Fission is splitting a large, heavy nucleus, while fusion is joining two smaller nuclei together. One breaks things apart, the other builds them up.
asks: Can you compare the two processes?
What is the difference between splitting and joining atoms?

faq.q: Do all stars run on fusion?
faq.a: The main sequence stars, like our Sun, primarily generate energy through the fusion of hydrogen into helium. This process is what keeps them shining.
asks: Is fusion the only power source in stars?
What fuels a star like the Sun?

faq.q: How do nuclear reactors control the reaction?
faq.a: They use control rods, often made of materials that absorb neutrons. This keeps the chain reaction from running away too quickly.
asks: What stops a nuclear reaction from getting too big?
How do we keep fission safe in a reactor?

faq.q: Is fusion possible on Earth right now?
faq.a: Scientists are working hard to make fusion happen controllably on Earth. It requires extremely high temperatures and pressures, which is very difficult.
asks: Can we build a fusion power plant soon?
What is the biggest challenge for fusion energy?

faq.q: What is the role of neutrons in these reactions?
faq.a: Neutrons are key because they can hit the nucleus to start fission, or they are released during the reaction to continue the chain. They are the messengers of the reaction.
asks: What do neutrons do in a chain reaction?

facts: Fission involves splitting heavy nuclei like Uranium-235.
Fusion involves combining light nuclei, such as isotopes of hydrogen.
Stars like the Sun generate energy primarily through hydrogen fusion.
A controlled chain reaction is what powers nuclear reactors.

quiz.say: Process A splits a large nucleus into smaller ones.
quiz.why: Fission is the process of splitting a large, unstable atomic nucleus into two or more smaller nuclei.

wrong.0: Combustion is burning, which is a chemical reaction, not a nuclear one.
wrong.1: Decay is a natural process, but fission specifically describes the splitting mechanism.
wrong.3: Fusion is the process of joining small nuclei together, which is the opposite action.

quiz.why: The Sun generates energy by fusing hydrogen atoms into helium atoms in its core.

wrong.0: Chemical burning releases energy through bonds, which is much less powerful than nuclear processes.
wrong.1: While decay happens, the primary, sustained energy source is fusion.
wrong.3: Fission requires heavy, unstable elements, which are not abundant in the Sun's core.

quiz.say: If a chain reaction is controlled, what is it used for?
quiz.why: Reactors use controlled fission chain reactions to safely produce heat, which then makes steam to turn turbines.

wrong.0: While advanced propulsion might use nuclear power, controlled reactors are designed for stationary power generation.
wrong.1: Stars start with gravitational collapse leading to fusion, not controlled fission.
wrong.2: Weapons use uncontrolled chain reactions, which is fundamentally different from the controlled process in a reactor.
